summary: Tokenize BASIC, read it back, print the syntax tree
description: Without further options, vcc basic translates a native BASIC program (line numbers optional, jump labels @name) into the storage format of the target system: PRG on Commodore, SAVE format (.bas) on Atari. The forms --tokenize and --detokenize work on the token level only. vcc basic ast prints the syntax tree.
The files are in the data folder. vcc finds it through --data-dir, VC_DATA, the location of the program or the working folder.

Read the source text as native BASIC, even with an extension other than .bas, .lst and .tur.

Switch off individual warnings, codes separated by commas (e.g. B150,B154). Errors cannot be switched off.

examples.title: Translate a C64 program with jump labels
Translate Turbo BASIC XL
examples.cmd: vcc basic examples/atari/turbo_basic/balken.tur --target atari8 --dialect turbo_basic_xl -o balken.bas

notes: #include brings in files and media (e.g. #include "graphics/hero.vcsprite" as DATA; project folder = nearest folder with a project file); media are read during conversion (--to-labels, --to-numbers, --renumber) but never written back.

Directives in native BASIC: #define NAME value (replacement before numbering), #if SYSTEM_C64 / #else / #endif, #dialect <id> (dialect of this file) and #asm "file.asm" [with "song.asm"] (machine code behind the BASIC text or as DATA lines; the symbols appear in the program as asm.name).
The output lists the labels (@name = line n) and, with #longnames, the mapping of the long names. A .sbas file is rejected.

The options -I, --pack, --map and --labels only work when translating source text with an extension other than .bas, .lst and .tur without --plain. For native BASIC they are accepted but not used. The option -D also works for native BASIC (like a #define).

forms.summary: show hex suggestions for chip register addresses or apply selected ones

args.name: datei
args.help: Native BASIC with decimal addresses (e.g. an imported program).

options.help: Switches to this form.
Target system (file in data/targets). It sets the dialect and the known chip registers.
BASIC dialect (file in data/basic).
Folder with the hardware database (data).
options.default_text: VC_DATA or next to the program

options.help: Numbers of the suggestions (from the list, separated by commas) to write to the output file. Without --apply, the suggestions are only listed. Nothing is ever changed without a selection.
Output file for --apply (the source file is never overwritten).

notes: Only complete decimal addresses from 256 upward are suggested, as an argument of POKE, PEEK, SYS, WAIT and USR, and only if they are a chip register of the target system. Arithmetic expressions, DATA and strings are left untouched.

Convert to line numbers and overwrite the file

notes: The mode of a file follows from its content; a mix of numbers and labels (B160) can be resolved with either conversion.
The names of manually assigned labels are kept as a line ;@name before the statement and reused when converting back.

forms.summary: print the syntax tree of a BASIC program

args.name: file.bas
args.help: BASIC source text (the same reader as in basic2asm).

options.help: Target system. It sets the BASIC dialect.
Read the source text as Turbo BASIC XL (target atari8 only).
Folder with the hardware database (data).
options.default_text: VC_DATA or next to the program

options.help: Print the tree as JSON (lines, statements, expressions; strings as byte lists).
options.default_text: Rust debug output of the lines

options.help: Print the tree as canonical text, read it back and report E191 if the tree is not the same. Takes precedence over --json.

notes: The call uses the parser of basic2asm. Its other options (-o, --map, --stage, --float, --int-div, --style, --runtime, --no-track-line, --no-rem, --check) are accepted but have no effect here.
Statements that the converter does not translate (OPEN, LOAD ...) cannot be written back (E190).

exit.0: tree printed, or round trip OK
exit.1: error in the source text, or round trip not OK
